record.goal: Build the scan carrier, the next carrier in the PAIR-CARRIER-SERVICES-001 family: it mounts established open-source security tools -- the twelve named in the operative text (Strix, Cloudflare Security Audit Skill, Trivy, Nuclei, Infisical, TruffleHog, NVIDIA SkillSpector, Semgrep, OpenAI Codex Security, Anthropic Claude Code Security Review, Microsoft PyRIT, Comp AI) -- as executors inside the 0R10N15 crossing, so every run of every tool issues its receipt pair at commit time: tool identity and version, ruleset version, target identity at run time, findings AND exclusions, verdict. The tools keep their names on every finding; the carrier claims no finding of its own and adds what the tools discard -- the contemporaneous state under which the finding was produced. The public track record of receipted runs is both the tools' advertisement and the standard record a security decision can be reconstructed from; revenue is per crossing, finding or clean alike. Proven specimen-first on the ecosystem's own surfaces (SkillSpector over its own skills; TruffleHog over its own public history, findings as predicates, never secret values), then opened to the twelve projects under an open invitation: mounting under license, declining free and public. The operative text is the queue item in the Ecosystem KV (QUEUE__WORK__SCAN_CARRIER__01, Drive 1QEX-omIcH4c0M-sJGSKxdqFa2RIOoumE, MD5 3f45337b826eebc6a6e6bb9945e5f92f). Work items: K-1 carrier core; K-2 SkillSpector specimen; K-3 TruffleHog specimen; K-4 mounting records per tool; K-5 the track-record surface; K-6 the open invitation; K-7 the merge-gate specimen (on K-2/K-3). Discharge per item is its named evidence read back; a fixture run discharges K-1 only. Failure filing: six-field non-ALLOW; first claim owns each item.
